title: Grothendieck rings of complex fusion categories: rank 2
summary: Recovers the two possible Grothendieck rings of complex fusion categories of rank two through sphericalization and central induction.
verification: Computer-free proof. The manuscript and editable source are available.

title: Grothendieck rings of complex fusion categories: rank 3
summary: Shows that every complex fusion category of rank three is spherical and recovers the five possible Grothendieck rings using moments of central twists.
verification: Computer-free proof. The quadratic-factor descent invokes Ostrik’s theorem.

title: Grothendieck rings of complex fusion categories: rank 4
summary: Proves sphericality in rank four using an exact finite search, then obtains the fifteen Grothendieck rings from the pivotal classification of Dong, Palcoux and Plessis.
verification: Computer-assisted proof, with exact code, input data and a one-command replay.

title: Invariant tensor dimensions as Hamburger moments
summary: Characterizes when invariant tensor dimensions form Hamburger moment sequences through a Cauchy–Schwarz criterion, with consequences for block structure, unimodularity and semisimplicity in finite tensor categories, and a related Stieltjes criterion.
verification: Prepared with ChatGPT and Claude; the Hexagon record reports partial human checking.

title: A Universal Square-Root-of-Six Bound for Kissing Numbers
summary: Establishes √6 as the optimal universal exponential base for Euclidean kissing numbers, with two elementary proofs independent of numerical tables. Equality holds only in dimension two.
verification: The Lean 4/Mathlib certificate registered in Palomar covers the volume proof, the planar value six and optimality of the base. The manuscript proves uniqueness of the equality dimension.

title: Prime factors of fusion-category dimensions: weak group-theoreticity, rank and decomposition
authors: Sebastian Burciu, Jingcheng Dong and Sébastien Palcoux
summary: Develops prime-factor criteria for weak group-theoreticity and decomposition of fusion categories. A non-pointed simple integral modular fusion category must have rank at least 32; the bounds are 33 in nonsquare dimension, 57 in odd dimension, and 75 in odd nonsquare dimension.
verification: Code, input data, calculation manifests, and explicit certificates are published in the verification repository.

title: Low-rank Grothendieck rings: an AI-assisted classification project, constructions, and open problems
summary: Explores which low-rank fusion rings admit fusion categories over the complex numbers, with constructions, exclusion arguments, open cases, and computational data.
verification: AI-generated research · independent verification pending. Results and computations remain provisional.
